sentences.text:
ORDER Applicant has filed this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973.

He is in jail since 18.3.2023 in connection with Crime No.1211/2022 registered at P.S. - Vijay Nagar, Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 376, 354, 354(a), 323,
294,

As per the prosecution story, on 28.9.2022 prosecutrix lodged an FIR at P.S. Vijay Nagar,
Indore by stating that she met the applicant in February 2020 and thereafter both liked each other and applicant proposed the prosecutrix for the marriage.
Thereafter with the consent of both the families, their marriage was arranged but later on dispute arose between them that applicant established physical relationship with other girls.
Then their marriage was broken.
Applicant threatened and beaten the prosecutrix and used abusive words.

On the basis of the FIR, initially Vicky vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83261774/
1 offence under Section 354, 354(a), 323, 294, 506, 509 of IPC has been registered but later on after 3 months, on the basis of the statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., offence under Section 376 of IPC has been additionally added.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He is in custody since 18.3.2023.
Investigation is almost over.
Prosecutrix herself broke the marriage and FIR is about 20 days belated.
Statement of the prosecutrix has been recorded after a period of about 3 months without any explanation for the delay.
Father of the applicant made complaint before the Counselor, Bhopal regarding the blackmailing done by the prosecutrix and her family.
Prosecutrix is a major lady.
Applicant is a permanent resident of District Bhopal.
His marriage has been settled with the other girl and is going to solemnize on 27.4.2023.
Hence, he prays that applicant be released on bail.

Per-contra, learned counsel for the objector opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix has supported the FIR in her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.,
applicant and his family Signature Notmembers Verified are still threatening the prosecutrix and her family members and if the Signed by: TRILOK SINGH applicant is released on bail, he would tamper the evidence.
Hence he prays that SAVNER Signing time: 21-Apr-23 2:48:01 PM the applicant does not deserve for bail.
Learned GA for respondent/State also opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection, but he fairly admits that no criminal antecedent has been found against the applicant.
Perused the case diary as well as the impugned order of the court below.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, nature and gravity of allegation as also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix is a 29 years old major lady, earlier her marriage was settled with the present applicant but due to some dispute marriage could not be performed, initially offence under Section 354, 354(a), 323, 294, 506, 509 of IPC was registered and later on offence under Section 376 IPC has been added after 3 months of registration of the offence,
FIR is also 20 days belated, investigation is almost over, in view of the above, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/-
with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S.
437(3) Cr.P.C.
C.C. as per rules.
